fact: China mined about 83% of the world’s tungsten in 2024. Tungsten is used for penetrators, fragmentation and the carbide cutting tools every machine shop runs on.
Leading-edge logic chips are made mostly in Taiwan. The exact share is not verified here.
The US produced no titanium sponge in 2025. The last domestic plant closed in 2024, and about 44,000 tonnes were imported.
The US share of global circuit board production fell from over 30% in 2000 to 4%. China makes roughly 50% to 56% (2020).
Solar polysilicon and wafers are made overwhelmingly in China. The exact share is not verified here.
China produced 99% of the world’s gallium in 2024. China banned exports to the US in Dec 2024, then paused the ban until Nov 27, 2026.
China made 94% of the world’s permanent magnets and did 91% of rare earth refining in 2024.
The US had only 2 operating primary copper smelters in 2025.
China produced 97% of the world’s battery anode materials in 2023.
China produced 59% of refined germanium in 2023 and put it under the same export ban as gallium.
China mined about 60% of the world’s antimony in 2024 (USGS estimate) and included it in the 2024 export ban. Antimony goes into primers and munitions.
Imports were an estimated 80% of US power transformer supply in 2025. Utilities wait 2 to 4 years, and up to 5.
US manufacturing could need up to 3.8 million new workers from 2024 to 2033, and 1.9 million of those jobs could go unfilled.
Turbine-grade nickel superalloy castings come from a small number of suppliers. Concentration is widely reported but not verified with a figure here.

Ammonium perchlorate, the oxidizer in solid rocket motors, has one qualified US producer (AMPAC, Utah). Solid rocket motor makers shrank from six to two between 1995 and 2017. The US has not made TNT since 1986; the Army awarded $435M for a Repkon USA plant in Kentucky.
The US government has long worried that Russia has a monopoly on HALEU. Centrus, the only US producer, is at demonstration scale: 20 kg delivered in Phase I, with a 900 kg target in Phase II.
US hypersonic flight tests are scarce and expensive, which slows each design iteration. This is a qualitative judgment.
